title: Check if Grid can be Cut into Sections
summary: Given an n x n grid and a set of non-overlapping rectangles, determine if it's possible to make either two horizontal or two vertical cuts such that each of the three resulting sections contains at least one rectangle, and every rectangle is in exactly one section.
statement: Given an n x n grid and a set of non-overlapping rectangles, determine if it's possible to make either two horizontal or two vertical cuts such that each of the three resulting sections contains at least one rectangle, and every rectangle is in exactly one section. Return true if possible, otherwise false.
constraints: The grid side n may reach one billion; at least three axis-aligned rectangles are pairwise non-overlapping.
Choose two horizontal or two vertical full-grid cuts that do not cross a rectangle.
Each of the three resulting sections must contain at least one whole rectangle.
hints: Cuts along one axis depend only on rectangle projections onto that axis.
Merge overlapping projections and count separated interval groups.
Sort starts; begin a new group when the next start is at least the current merged end; test for three groups.
A cut can lie between every two consecutive merged groups, so two cuts exist exactly when some axis has at least three groups.
editorial: A cut can lie between every two consecutive merged groups, so two cuts exist exactly when some axis has at least three groups.

tests.explanation: Horizontal boundaries separate the rectangles into three nonempty bands.
Neither axis has three separable interval groups, so two valid cuts do not exist.
